Command: Do Good to All, Especially the Household of Faith
Summary: Paul's doing-good command: as we have opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
Commandment: As we have therefore opportunity, let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
Application: The circle is wide — all men — with a centre — the household of faith. Opportunity is the occasion: good is done as doors open, not postponed until a grander occasion arrives.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to order generosity outward from the church without confining it there.
Function: The circle is wide — all men — with a centre: the household of faith. Not Mosaic law but apostolic teaching — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal, on the TRADITIONAL reading, was to order generosity outward from the church without confining it there. The evil it addressed was good postponed — help withheld until a grander occasion arrives, or confined to insiders only. It restrained that evil by the occasion itself: as we have opportunity, let us do good unto all men.
